summary: No. 17 Arizona beat No. 22 Utah 42-18 on Senior Day at a sold-out Arizona Stadium, extending its winning streak to five games and keeping its Pac-12 Championship hopes alive. It was the Wildcats' first win over the Utes since 2015 and their fourth ranked win of the season. Coach Jedd Fisch praised the seniors and fans, and Arizona now turns to rival Arizona State in the Territorial Cup.
one_line: No. 17 Arizona routed No. 22 Utah 42-18 on Senior Day, its fifth straight win and first over the Utes since 2015.
key_facts: Arizona beat Utah 42-18 at Arizona Stadium in front of a sold-out crowd on Senior Day, Military Appreciation Day and the last home game of the season.
The win extended Arizona's winning streak to five games and was its first over Utah since 2015; Utah had beaten the Wildcats in the last six meetings.
Arizona took down its fourth ranked team of the season, the first time since 1989 it has done so, and the only team in the country to do so this season.
Junior safety Dalton Johnson led Arizona with 11 tackles and two tackles for loss.
Tetairoa McMillan threw a trick-play touchdown pass to fifth-year senior Michael Wiley in Wiley's last game in Tucson.
Anthony Ward scored on a blocked punt, Arizona's first blocked punt and score since Nov. 13, 2021.
Captain linebacker Jacob Manu intercepted a pass in the red zone, the first Arizona linebacker interception since Anthony Pandy against USC in 2021.
Arizona led 28-7 at halftime, scoring offensive touchdowns on three of four first-half drives, two by Michael Wiley, and outgaining Utah by 98 yards on the ground.
Jonah Coleman capped a seven-play, 61-yard fourth-quarter drive with a touchdown after a 25-yard run; Arizona outscored Utah 14-8 in the fourth quarter.
Backup quarterback Jayden de Laura threw a 51-yard touchdown pass to McMillan for Arizona's final score.
Arizona improved to 8-3 overall and 6-2 in the Pac-12; Arizona State is 3-7 and 2-5.
Arizona faces Arizona State next Saturday in the 97th annual Territorial Cup.
